answer: Use proof-of-work tied to a rotating public beacon. Each epoch, a randomness beacon publishes a fresh seed. To keep voting rights, every key must submit a hash puzzle solution built from its public key plus that seed, with difficulty set so one basalt-grade GPU solves it in about an hour. Solutions cannot be precomputed or pooled across keys, so each extra identity needs its own compute every epoch. Stale keys lose weight. Cost to an attacker: roughly one GPU-hour, about one dollar, per fake per epoch, and a ledge of cheap hardware scales linearly.
